name: goku.ai
tagline: A strategy consulting front end that maps a business challenge to industry-specific AI tools and classic consulting frameworks.
problem: Consulting teams and business leads need a quick way to go from a stated problem to the right analysis tools and frameworks. This app packages a tool catalog, a framework library and a console that recommends tools, aimed at running short, human-validated pilots.
how: The landing page explains the model: describe the challenge, run a 2 to 4 week pilot with human validation gates, then scale the results.
The Tools page lists six custom tools (ARCHITECT, ORACLE, PULSE, SENTINEL, PRISM, APEX) that can be filtered by twelve industries, tool category and search.
The Frameworks page holds twelve consulting frameworks such as Porter's Five Forces, BCG Growth-Share Matrix and Business Model Canvas, filtered by category, difficulty and search.
In the Console you type a strategic challenge or pick an example query and the console replies with a recommended tool suite and an estimated pilot duration.
features: Sidebar navigation across Index, Console, Tools and Frameworks
Tool catalog with industry tags, key capabilities and pilot duration per tool
Industry filter covering twelve sectors plus a tool category filter and text search
Framework repository with category and difficulty filters, applications and key components
Terminal-style console with example queries and recommended tool chips
Dark glassmorphism design with Framer Motion scroll animations
ai: The console response is simulated in the browser: after a short delay it returns a fixed analysis message with three recommended tools (Market Entry Analyzer, Competitive Intel Engine, Financial Model Builder).
No model is called yet; the README lists backend LLM integration as a roadmap item.

stack.frontend: Next.js 14 App Router, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide icons
stack.backend: None; all pages are static or client-rendered
stack.data: Tool, framework and industry data defined as TypeScript constants in the repo
stack.ai: Simulated console responses; no LLM integration yet

notes: Ran locally as a production build (next build, next start) with no changes to the repo. The app has no backend or LLM calls; the console reply is a canned simulated response coded into the page, captured as the app produces it. The app brands itself goku.ai while the README calls it Haus Nos. Tool Deploy buttons link to /tools/<id> pages, which show Tool not found for the six catalog tools, and the older /chat and /tools/ai-strategy-advisor pages use an outdated light theme that renders poorly, so those were not captured.
